label: prop:bar-parity-split
title: Binding (cosh) and β-decay (sinh) are the two bar-parities of one element
html:
Proposition. Binding (cosh) and β-decay (sinh) are the two bar-parities of one element

The bar-involution \sigma defined by q \mapsto q^{-1} and \sigma^2 = \mathrm{id} (def:bar-involution) splits any element x into a \sigma-fixed even part and a \sigma-anti odd part:

\mathrm{even}(x) = x + \sigma x, \qquad
\mathrm{odd}(x) = x - \sigma x, \qquad
\mathrm{even}(x) + \mathrm{odd}(x) = 2x.

Applying this to the fibre Habiro element F that controls the substrate separates the two observables:

  • even (\cosh, bar-symmetric): The binding trace \tau = \mathrm{tr}\, B from prop:sl2-prolongation-recurrence. This is the curvature-free transport, (q+q^{-1})/2 = \cosh\lambda.
  • odd (\sinh, bar-antisymmetric): The \mathfrak{Q}_\beta residue-A / c_k ladder. This is the curvature defect, (q-q^{-1})/2 = \sinh\lambda, representing the bar-odd Habiro dual of \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}.

Binding (mass-average) and \beta-decay (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta) represent the even and odd parities of a single bar-graded element. Pinning either parity constrains the other.

The bar-even/bar-odd split corresponds to the real/imaginary split of the complex volume \mathfrak{V} (conj:binding-qbeta-complex-volume). The continuation \lambda \mapsto i\theta sends \cosh\lambda \mapsto \cos\theta and \sinh\lambda \mapsto i\sin\theta. The bar-even part becomes \mathrm{Re}\,\mathfrak{V} = \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} and the bar-odd part becomes \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V} = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta. The additive projections x \mapsto x \pm \sigma x permit a single identity on \mathfrak{V} to descend to both channels simultaneously.

Mapping this algebraic decomposition to the physical dichotomy of binding and decay provides a rigorous interpretive framework for the Quantum Observable Universe.
